intro: Look up. You are standing before the Column of Constantine in İstanbul province, raised in AD 330. When Constantine founded his new capital, he set this porphyry column at the centre of his forum. It is the city's oldest standing monument, and it has stood in the same place for seventeen centuries.
history: When Constantine founded his new capital in 330, he set this column of porphyry drums at the centre of his forum and placed his own statue on top. The statue came down in a storm in 1106. The shaft, blackened by fires, was strengthened with iron hoops — and that is where its Turkish name comes from.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the porphyry drums and the iron hoops, then the Ottoman repair base and the area of the old forum around you.
facts: Did you know? This is the oldest standing monument in the city: raised two centuries before Hagia Sophia and thirteen before the Blue Mosque. Constantine set the column at the centre of his forum in 330 and crowned it with his own statue, which came down in a storm in 1106.
outro: This brings our visit to the Column of Constantine to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This column has stood for seventeen centuries; let it keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
